text: Continuous Integration (CI) is a common practice in modern software development. Developers regularly add their code to a shared repository, and each change triggers automated builds. This means the software is compiled and checked without anyone doing it by hand. As part of the process, running tests happens automatically too. These tests help in catching issues early, before they become big problems. A CI pipeline usually includes steps like building, testing, and reporting results. If something fails, the team knows immediately and can fix it quickly. By using CI pipelines, teams save time, reduce mistakes, and keep their projects healthy and ready for release.
